correctness.rationale: At positive spatial diffusivity and bounded propulsion the stopped Girsanov derivative is justified for sufficiently small force. The force score on a fixed exit event has a constant endpoint part, which cancels under conditioning, leaving minus one-half the propulsion strength times the time--orientation-integral covariance. Reflection at zero bias reduces the directional difference to one such covariance. Four backward Dirichlet equations for the indicator, its time integral, the orientation integral and their product yield the explicit H/K resolvent hierarchy in RESULT.md. Elementary Green integration gives the closed rational-hyperbolic coefficient, checked against independent quadrature at six diffusivities and a direct coupled harmonic boundary-value discretization at four. The exponential variable y=exp(-1/(2 sqrt(epsilon))) gives the exact leading two algebraic powers and exponentially small error. This is an analytic proof, not an inference from finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly bounds but leaves undetermined the leading directional difference of the quadratic-activity conditional-time coefficients. This result computes the zero-force derivative of that same difference, gives its exact finite-diffusivity expression, and resolves a leading cancellation to exhibit a 1/(12 epsilon) term rather than the weaker O(epsilon^(-3/2)) bound. Prior work on passive symmetry, one-wall active first passage, parabolic-barrier propagation and chiral splitting probabilities neither states this susceptibility nor supplies its coefficient without further nontrivial analysis. The source equations and general perturbation tools are acknowledged; originality is assigned only to the exact evaluated response and sharp asymptotic, with implicit general-coverage risk recorded.

value.rationale: The difference between bias-conditioned uphill and downhill mean first-passage times is a natural and directly observable nonequilibrium timing asymmetry. The closest source explicitly identifies its undetermined boundary-layer remainder. Resolving the infinitesimal-bias limit with an exact formula, its leading 1/(12 epsilon) coefficient and an exponentially sharp two-term expansion supplies the missing physical scale and uncovers cancellation of the larger order suggested by available estimates. This is not a renamed passive identity or a numerically selected arbitrary parameter slice; zero force is the natural linear-response point.
